h: Three Voices of Rebuke That Draw Israel Near

p: is always read before Tisha B'Av.
according to what is written in the Midrash
(רֵישׁ אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי, אֵיכָה רַבָּה א, א)
(at the beginning of Eichah Rabbah, Eichah Rabbah 1:1):
is said of Moshe and Aharon,
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 53b):
"Moshe is the groomsman of the King,
Aharon is the groomsman of the Matronisa."
is called the groomsman of the King,
for he brought HaKadosh Baruch Hu close to Yisrael.
whose entire intent and service was
and to instill the words of Torah
"Be among the disciples of Aharon, etc.,
and bringing them close to Torah."
was also the groomsman of the Matronisa,
but his main name and aspect
is the groomsman of the King,
in that he brought the Torah down to Yisrael.
Now here, in the Midrash mentioned above,
which likened Moshe, Yeshayahu and Yirmiyahu
its intent is that all of them
And it says in the Midrash:
in their glory and their tranquility,
וְאָמַר אֵיכָה אֶשָּׂא לְבַדִּי וְכוּלֵּי (דְּבָרִים א, יב)
and said, 'How can I bear alone' (Devarim 1:12)," etc.
That is: he brought Yisrael close
like the stars of the heavens in multitude";
that they are great like the stars,
in the sense of what is said (Daniel 12:3):
"And those who bring the many to righteousness, like the stars";
and in the manner of what it says (Megillah 16a):
they rise up to the stars."
And even though they said this
in stature and level like stars.
וְאָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, said to them:
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאַתֶּם גְּדוֹלִים בְּמַעֲלָה כָּל כָּךְ
since you are so great in stature,
that you do not lower yourselves
and do not fall, chas v'shalom,
And this groomsman brought them close
to bring them close to Hashem Yisbarach
how have you fallen from heaven to earth,
and do not bring about punishment,
"And Yirmiyahu saw them in their disgrace"
that is, after they had already been punished;
to bring them close through this
in the manner of what is said (Yirmiyahu 30:17):
"And from your wounds I will heal you";
and through this they will draw close
(as is written in the Yerushalmi, Berachos,
That is, he brought them close to Hashem Yisbarach
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה ד, כה)
and as they said (Midrash Rabbah Eichah 4:25):
"The scroll of Lamentations was better for Yisrael
And for this reason we read on this Shabbos
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and in the haftarah, "The vision of Yeshayahu,"
for all of them are called groomsmen,

p: there is a revelation of Atika,
meaning that they are bound at the root,
and they are "like the stars of the heavens";
and this corresponds to the rebuke
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
And at the beginning of Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu
"But to this one I will look:
to the poor and broken of spirit,
for they are in the aspect of poor
for on Shabbos a Jew becomes
מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה נֶגֶד רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
what he did against His will, may His Name be blessed.
And Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
and it says in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer:
'But he who confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy'";
and "even one who worships idols like Enosh
and this corresponds to the rebuke of Yirmiyahu.
is in the aspect of a talmid chacham,
And likewise it is expounded in the holy Zohar
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and from your trembling
as referring to the day of Shabbos,
since it is written "on the day that He gives rest"
And the meaning of "from your sorrow":
what he is sorrowful about the past;
from the turmoil of the yetzer hara
to be saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
as is written in the Mechilta
"And keeps his hand from doing any evil"
that he is guarded from sin;
and in Pri Etz Chaim it is stated
that he is saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara;
and this corresponds to the rebuke of Yeshayahu,
who saw them in their recklessness.
for on Shabbos a Jew has
in the midst of the hard labor,
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach,
and He looks only toward good;
"And from your wounds I will heal you"
the rebukes of the three groomsmen
so that we draw close through all of them
amen, may it be His will.
